claims.text: XPS can enhance oxidation resistance in metals or alloys.
XPS can provide in situ characterization for oxidation monitoring.
The proposed starting material is a polycrystalline metal or alloy.
The intervention is the application of XPS to monitor oxidation states in situ.
The proposed oxidation environment is above 500 °C.
The proposed oxidation environment has controlled oxygen partial pressure.
Oxide-layer formation and growth mediate the proposed response.
Real-time XPS monitoring can detect the early stages of oxidation.
Detection of early oxidation enables optimization of oxidation-resistant coatings or surface treatments.
XPS monitoring will produce a 30% reduction in oxidation rate relative to the baseline.
Oxidation rate is measured as oxide-layer thickness in nanometers per hour.
The baseline is an untreated polycrystalline metal or alloy exposed to the same high-temperature environment.
The effectiveness of XPS may depend on the particular metal or alloy system.
The effectiveness of XPS may depend on the experimental conditions.

contradictions.description: The intervention consists only of XPS monitoring, but the mechanism attributes resistance improvement to optimization of coatings or surface treatments that are not included in the intervention. Thus, the stated intervention does not itself provide the treatment needed to cause the predicted oxidation-rate reduction.

The boundary identifies reductions both below 20% and above 40%, whereas the falsification rule treats only a reduction below 20% as rate-based falsification and does not explain how a reduction above 40% should be interpreted.
